questions.text: Fossa for lacrimal gland is situated at the …… of the orbit.
questions.explanation: At the lateral part of the roof.
questions.keyConcept: Roof

questions.text: Which of the following nerves passes through the inferior orbital fissure?
questions.explanation: The other nerves pass through the superior orbital fissure.
questions.keyConcept: Zygomatic

questions.text: A nerve crossing the superior orbital fissure within the tendinous ring is:
questions.explanation: The other nerves pass outside the tendinous ring.
questions.keyConcept: Abducent

questions.text: The common tendinous ring is a thickening of:
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Periorbital fascia.
questions.keyConcept: Periorbital fascia

questions.text: The main ligament preventing inferior displacement of the eye ball is:
questions.explanation: It is a sling-like ligament below the eye ball.
questions.keyConcept: Suspensory

questions.text: One of the following muscles is attached behind the equator of the eye:
questions.explanation: Both oblique muscles are inserted behind the equator of the eye.
questions.keyConcept: Superior oblique

questions.text: One of the following muscles is attached to the floor of the orbit:
questions.explanation: It originates from the floor of the orbit.
questions.keyConcept: Inferior oblique

questions.text: Looking straight upwards is performed by …… muscle.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Superior rectus.
questions.keyConcept: Superior rectus

questions.text: Looking to the ipsilateral shoulder is performed by …… muscle.
questions.explanation: It performs depression, abduction, and intorsion.
questions.keyConcept: Ipsilateral superior oblique

questions.text: Looking upwards and laterally is performed by …… muscles.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Superior rectus and inferior oblique.
questions.keyConcept: Superior rectus and inferior oblique

questions.text: The following muscles help the lateral rectus in abduction of the eye:
questions.explanation: Both oblique muscles perform abduction of the eye.
questions.keyConcept: Superior oblique and inferior oblique

questions.text: Horner's syndrome includes all the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Partial ptosis (only the tarsal part of LPS is paralyzed here).
questions.keyConcept: Complete ptosis
options: Inward displacement of the eye ball

questions.text: The superior division of oculomotor nerve supplies …… muscle.
questions.explanation: The superior division also supplies the superior rectus muscle.
questions.keyConcept: Levator palpebrae

questions.text: Inability to look to the right shoulder denotes injury of …… nerve.
questions.explanation: The left trochlear nerve supplies the right superior oblique muscle, which is responsible for depression, abduction, and intorsion (to look to the ipsilateral shoulder) — remember the trochlear nerve decussation.
questions.keyConcept: Left trochlear

questions.text: An artery accompanying the optic nerve within the optic canal is:
questions.explanation: It is inferolateral to the nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Ophthalmic

questions.text: The optic nerve is crossed from lateral to medial by …… nerve.
questions.explanation: The ophthalmic artery and superior ophthalmic vein also cross the optic nerve from lateral to medial.
questions.keyConcept: Nasociliary

questions.text: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers controlling sphincter pupillae are derived from …… nucleus.
questions.explanation: It is the parasympathetic nucleus of the oculomotor nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Edinger-Westphal

questions.text: Which of the following arteries anastomoses with facial artery?
questions.explanation: It is one of the terminal branches of the ophthalmic artery, forming an anastomosis between the external and internal carotid arteries.
questions.keyConcept: Dorsal nasal

questions.text: The lacrimal duct drains into the …… of the nasal cavity.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Inferior meatus.
questions.keyConcept: Inferior meatus

questions.text: The lacrimal nerve receives postganglionic parasympathetic fibers to lacrimal gland through …… nerve.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Zygomatico-temporal.
questions.keyConcept: Zygomatico-temporal

questions.text: The 2nd order neuron of the visual pathway is:
questions.explanation: Their axons form the optic nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Ganglion cells of the retina

questions.text: The right optic tract carries …… retinal fibers.
questions.explanation: Nasal fibers cross within the optic chiasma while temporal fibers remain uncrossed.
questions.keyConcept: Right temporal and left nasal

questions.text: Pituitary tumor compressing the center of the optic chiasma may cause:
questions.explanation: It affects the nasal fibers of both sides (responsible for the temporal fields of vision).
questions.keyConcept: Bitemporal hemianopia

questions.text: An aneurysm of right ICA compressing the lateral part of the optic chiasma may cause:
questions.explanation: It affects the temporal fibers responsible for the nasal field of vision.
questions.keyConcept: Right nasal hemianopia

questions.text: Afferent impulses of the corneal reflex are carried by …… nerve.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Ophthalmic.
questions.keyConcept: Ophthalmic

questions.text: Which of the following is derived from mesoderm?
questions.explanation: The other structures are derived from neuro-ectoderm.
questions.keyConcept: Sclera

questions.text: The optic vesicle appears at the end of …… week.
questions.explanation: It appears from the side of the forebrain.
questions.keyConcept: 4th

questions.text: Failure of closure of the choroid fissure leads to:
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Coloboma iridis.
questions.keyConcept: Coloboma iridis
options: Strands in front of the pupil

questions.text: The lower 1/3 of the auricle is supplied by …… nerve.
questions.explanation: It supplies both the medial and lateral surfaces of the lower 1/3 of the auricle.
questions.keyConcept: Great auricular

questions.text: Choose the wrong statement about the external auditory meatus:
questions.explanation: Its cartilaginous part is wider and shorter than the bony part.
questions.keyConcept: Its cartilaginous part is longer than its bony part.
options: It is lined by thin skin rich in waxy glands.
It is formed of outer cartilaginous and inner bony parts.
Its cartilaginous part is longer than its bony part.

questions.text: Posterior half of the external auditory meatus is supplied by …… nerve.
questions.explanation: Its anterior half is supplied by the auriculotemporal nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Auricular branch of vagus

questions.text: The inner veins of the tympanic membrane drain into:
questions.explanation: Its outer veins drain into the external jugular vein.
questions.keyConcept: Transverse sinus

questions.text: The inner surface of the tympanic membrane is supplied by …… nerve.
questions.explanation: Tonsillitis can cause ear pain (the tonsils are supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve).
questions.keyConcept: Tympanic branch of glossopharyngeal

questions.text: The floor of the tympanic cavity is related to:
questions.explanation: A thin plate of bone separates the internal jugular vein from the middle ear cavity, so infection of the middle ear can reach the IJV causing its thrombosis.
questions.keyConcept: Internal jugular vein

questions.text: Stapedius muscle originates from a bony projection in the …… of the tympanic cavity.
questions.explanation: This projection is called the pyramid.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior wall

questions.text: The facial nerve gives nerve to stapedius muscle while it crosses:
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Petrous temporal bone.
questions.keyConcept: Petrous temporal bone

questions.text: Lax tympanic membrane denotes injury of …… nerve.
questions.explanation: Paralysis of the tensor tympani, which is supplied by the mandibular nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Mandibular

questions.text: The epitympanic recess contains:
questions.explanation: The head of the malleus articulates with the body of the incus here.
questions.keyConcept: Head of malleus and body of incus
options: Head of malleus and body of incus
Body of incus and head of stapes
Long and short processes of incus

questions.text: The auditory tube begins at the …… wall of the tympanic cavity.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Anterior.
questions.keyConcept: Anterior

questions.text: The otic vesicle develops from the:
questions.explanation: During the 4th week, from its caudal part.
questions.keyConcept: Rhombencephalon

questions.text: The cochlea develops in the …… week.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: 6th.
questions.keyConcept: 6th

questions.text: The lining epithelium of the auditory tube is derived from:
questions.explanation: From the tubo-tympanic recess of the 1st pharyngeal pouch.
questions.keyConcept: 1st pharyngeal pouch

questions.text: Which of the following develops from cartilage of the 2nd pharyngeal arch?
questions.explanation: The malleus and incus develop from the cartilage of the 1st pharyngeal arch.
questions.keyConcept: Stapes

questions.text: The meatal plug of the fetal ear usually dissolves in the …… month.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: 7th.
questions.keyConcept: 7th

questions.text: Which of the following shares in the nasal septum?
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Perpendicular plate of ethmoid.
questions.keyConcept: Perpendicular plate of ethmoid

questions.text: Superior and middle nasal conchae are parts of …… bone.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Ethmoid.
questions.keyConcept: Ethmoid

questions.text: The facial artery supplies …… quadrant of the nasal cavity.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Antero-inferior.
questions.keyConcept: Antero-inferior

questions.text: Anterior superior alveolar nerve supplies …… quadrant of the nasal cavity.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Antero-inferior.
questions.keyConcept: Antero-inferior

questions.text: Which of the following air sinuses drains into superior nasal meatus?
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Posterior ethmoidal.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior ethmoidal

questions.text: Infection of which paranasal sinus will reach the retropharyngeal lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: Posterior ethmoidal and sphenoidal sinuses drain into the retropharyngeal lymph nodes.
questions.keyConcept: Sphenoidal

questions.text: Ala of the nose develops from …… prominence.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: Lateral nasal.
questions.keyConcept: Lateral nasal

questions.text: The olfactory epithelium lines the whole …… of the nasal cavity.
questions.explanation: With slight extension to the medial and lateral walls.
questions.keyConcept: Roof

questions.text: The 2ry olfactory cortex lies within:
questions.explanation: The entorhinal area (area 28).
questions.keyConcept: Para-hippocampal gyrus

questions.text: The larynx extends between …… vertebrae.
questions.explanation: Per the official answer key, the correct answer is: C4-C6.
questions.keyConcept: C4-C6

questions.text: Facial nerve injury leads to loss of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The facial nerve is the efferent (motor to orbicularis oculi) limb of the corneal reflex, so its injury abolishes the blink. The trigeminal nerve provides the afferent limb and corneal sensation, while the light and accommodation reflexes use the optic and oculomotor nerves.
questions.keyConcept: Facial nerve is the efferent limb of the corneal (blink) reflex

questions.text: A lesion in the pretectal nucleus leads to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The pretectal nucleus is the center of the pupillary light reflex. Lens curvature and the near response depend on the oculomotor and Edinger-Westphal pathway, squint reflects extraocular muscle imbalance, and field defects follow optic pathway lesions.
questions.keyConcept: The pretectal nucleus is the center of the light reflex

questions.text: Which nerve carries the motor parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion?
questions.explanation: The parasympathetic (motor) root of the ciliary ganglion travels with the nerve to the inferior oblique, a branch of the oculomotor nerve.
questions.keyConcept: The parasympathetic root of the ciliary ganglion runs with the nerve to inferior oblique

questions.text: The following is the action of the superior oblique muscle:
questions.explanation: From the primary position the superior oblique muscle produces depression, intorsion and abduction; its principal actions tested clinically are depression and intorsion.
questions.keyConcept: The superior oblique produces depression and intorsion

questions.text: Which of the following does not share in the development of the eyeball?
questions.explanation: The eyeball develops from surface ectoderm (lens and corneal epithelium), neuroectoderm and the optic vesicle (retina and optic nerve), and mesoderm (sclera, choroid and vessels). Endoderm contributes no part of the eyeball.
questions.keyConcept: Endoderm does not contribute to development of the eyeball

questions.text: A lesion in which of the following nerves leads to loss of the corneal reflex?
questions.explanation: The trigeminal nerve is the afferent limb of the corneal reflex (stimulus: touching the cornea; center: midbrain; efferent: facial nerve; response: bilateral blinking).
questions.keyConcept: The trigeminal nerve is the afferent limb of the corneal reflex

questions.text: A lesion in the right optic tract results in which of the following?
questions.explanation: The right optic tract carries fibers from the right temporal and left nasal hemiretinae, representing the left visual field; its lesion causes a left homonymous hemianopia.
questions.keyConcept: Right optic tract lesion causes a left homonymous hemianopia

questions.text: A 50-year-old man complained of inability to see cars moving beside him while crossing the road. MRI revealed a pituitary tumor. What is the expected visual field defect?
questions.explanation: A pituitary adenoma compresses the crossing nasal fibers at the optic chiasma, producing loss of both temporal (peripheral) fields, a bitemporal hemianopia.
questions.keyConcept: Pituitary tumor compresses the chiasma, causing bitemporal hemianopia

questions.text: The lining epithelium of the tympanic cavity develops from the:
questions.explanation: The tympanic cavity and auditory tube are lined by epithelium derived from the endoderm of the 1st pharyngeal (tubotympanic) pouch.
questions.keyConcept: Tympanic cavity lining derives from the 1st pharyngeal pouch

questions.text: Which of the following lies in the medial wall of the middle ear cavity?
questions.explanation: The promontory, a bulge produced by the basal turn of the cochlea, lies on the medial wall of the middle ear. The pyramid is on the posterior wall, the auditory tube and carotid canal relate to the anterior wall, and the tegmen tympani forms the roof.
questions.keyConcept: The promontory lies on the medial wall of the middle ear

questions.text: The muscle that makes the eye look downwards and medially is the:
questions.explanation: From the primary position the inferior rectus depresses and adducts the eye, so it directs the gaze downwards and medially.
questions.keyConcept: The inferior rectus moves the eye downwards and medially

questions.text: The lateral olfactory stria terminates in the:
questions.explanation: The lateral olfactory stria carries olfactory fibers to the primary olfactory cortex (the uncus and adjacent piriform area).
questions.keyConcept: The lateral olfactory stria ends in the primary olfactory cortex

questions.text: Coloboma is a cleft in the:
questions.explanation: Coloboma results from failure of the choroid (optic) fissure to close during development; the typical inferonasal cleft is seen in the iris.
questions.keyConcept: Coloboma (failed optic-fissure closure) presents as a cleft in the iris

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT involved in the light reflex?
questions.explanation: The light reflex runs from retinal ganglion cells along the optic nerve to the pretectal area and then to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei. The lateral geniculate body belongs to the image-forming visual pathway, not the light reflex.
questions.keyConcept: The lateral geniculate body is not part of the light reflex arc

questions.text: Regarding the eyelids, one statement is false:
questions.explanation: Eyelid skin is the thinnest in the body and has no subcutaneous fat, so the statement that it is rich in fat is false. The eyelids do contain Moll (sweat) and Zeis (sebaceous) glands, the skeletal orbicularis oculi, and the tarsal plate.
questions.keyConcept: Eyelid skin is thin and has no subcutaneous fat (the false statement)
options: They contain sweat glands called Moll's glands
They contain sebaceous glands called Zeis glands
The orbicularis oculi is formed of skeletal muscle fibers
They are covered by thin skin rich in fat

questions.text: The branch of the facial nerve that arises from the geniculate ganglion is the:
questions.explanation: The greater petrosal nerve, carrying preganglionic parasympathetic fibers for lacrimation, branches from the facial nerve at the geniculate ganglion.
questions.keyConcept: The greater petrosal nerve arises at the geniculate ganglion

questions.text: Which of the following is involved in light reflexes?
questions.explanation: The pretectal nucleus is the midbrain center that mediates the pupillary light reflex.
questions.keyConcept: The pretectal nucleus mediates the pupillary light reflex

chapters.title: Histology
chapters.subtitle: Histology of the Eye and Ear

subjects.name: Histology
subjects.lectures: The Eye, The Ear, Structure of the Ear

questions.text: Limbus is:
questions.explanation: The limbus (corneoscleral junction) is the transition zone where the transparent cornea becomes the opaque sclera; it houses the trabecular meshwork and canal of Schlemm.
questions.keyConcept: Limbus = corneoscleral junction (transition zone between cornea & sclera).
options: The transition zone between cornea & sclera.
The transition zone between the iris & cornea.
The transition zone between the iris & ciliary body.

questions.text: Iridocorneal angle contains all these structures except:
questions.explanation: The iridocorneal (drainage) angle contains the trabecular meshwork with the spaces of Fontana, the canal of Schlemm and the pectinate ligament. Bowman's membrane is the anterior limiting layer of the cornea, not part of the angle.
questions.keyConcept: Iridocorneal angle holds spaces of Fontana, canal of Schlemm & pectinate ligament; NOT Bowman's membrane.

questions.text: Melanocytes are not present in:
questions.explanation: The cornea must stay transparent, so it is avascular and free of melanocytes. Melanocytes are found in the sclera (lamina fusca), iris and ciliary body.
questions.keyConcept: Melanocytes occur in sclera, iris & ciliary body but NOT in the transparent cornea.

questions.text: The most vascular part in the eye is:
questions.explanation: The choroid is the highly vascular, pigmented layer of the uvea; its choriocapillaris nourishes the outer retina, making it the most vascular part of the eye.
questions.keyConcept: The choroid is the most vascular coat of the eye.

questions.text: The inner layer of ciliary processes epithelium:
questions.explanation: The inner non-pigmented ciliary epithelium is an ion-transporting epithelium with basal membrane infoldings and many elongated mitochondria; it actively secretes the aqueous humour, so all options apply.
questions.keyConcept: Inner (non-pigmented) ciliary epithelium has basal infoldings & mitochondria and secretes aqueous humour.

questions.text: A structure not involved in visual accommodation:
questions.explanation: Accommodation changes lens shape through ciliary muscle contraction and zonular fibre tension. The retina is the photoreceptive layer and plays no mechanical role in accommodation.
questions.keyConcept: Accommodation involves lens, zonule & ciliary body; the retina is NOT involved.

questions.text: Which of these is not a true muscle:
questions.explanation: The dilator pupillae is formed of myoepithelial (myoid) processes of the anterior pigmented iris epithelium, so it is not a true smooth muscle. The constrictor pupillae and ciliary muscle are true smooth muscles.
questions.keyConcept: Dilator pupillae is myoepithelial (not a true muscle); constrictor pupillae & ciliary muscle are true smooth muscle.

questions.text: Bruch's membrane contains:
questions.explanation: Bruch's membrane is the innermost layer of the choroid; it is built of collagen layers around a central elastic-fibre core plus the basal laminae of the choriocapillaris and retinal pigment epithelium. Of the options, collagen fibers is correct.
questions.keyConcept: Bruch's membrane contains collagen fibers (with a central elastic core).

questions.text: The inner nuclear layer of the retina contains:
questions.explanation: The inner nuclear layer contains the cell bodies of the bipolar, horizontal, amacrine and Muller (glial) cells, so all of the listed cells are present.
questions.keyConcept: Inner nuclear layer holds nuclei of bipolar, horizontal, amacrine & Muller cells (all of the above).

questions.text: The outer blood-retinal barrier is made of:
questions.explanation: The outer blood-retinal barrier is formed by zonulae occludentes between the retinal pigment epithelial cells, isolating the outer retina from the fenestrated choriocapillaris. The inner barrier is formed by the retinal capillary endothelium.
questions.keyConcept: Outer blood-retinal barrier = tight junctions between retinal pigment epithelial cells.
options: Junctional complexes between processes of Muller cells & the photoreceptors.
Junctional complexes between pigmented epithelial cells.

questions.text: The cone cells are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Cone photoreceptors use the photopigment iodopsin and their membranous discs remain continuous with the plasma membrane (unlike rods, whose discs are separate and use rhodopsin). Hence answers b & c.
questions.keyConcept: Cones contain iodopsin and have discs continuous with the cell membrane (answers b & c).

questions.text: The inner plexiform layer contains:
questions.explanation: The inner plexiform layer is where the axons of bipolar cells synapse with ganglion and amacrine cell dendrites; the listed correct content is axons of bipolar cells.
questions.keyConcept: Inner plexiform layer = synapses of bipolar cell axons with ganglion/amacrine cells.

questions.text: Pigmented epithelial cells of the retina contain all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Retinal pigment epithelial cells show apical microvilli that ensheath photoreceptor outer segments, abundant SER for vitamin A metabolism, and basal membrane infoldings. Pinocytotic vesicles are not a listed feature.
questions.keyConcept: RPE cells have apical microvilli, SER & basal infoldings, but NOT pinocytotic vesicles.

questions.text: Optic disc is:
questions.explanation: The optic disc is where ganglion cell axons leave the eye and retinal vessels enter; it lacks photoreceptors (the blind spot) and so is insensitive to light. Maximum acuity is at the fovea, not the disc.
questions.keyConcept: Optic disc = blind spot: no photoreceptors, so it is insensitive to light.
options: The site of maximum visual acuity.
Where condensation of photoreceptors is found.

questions.text: Bulbar conjunctiva is lined by:
questions.explanation: Over the sclera the bulbar conjunctiva is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium (it becomes stratified columnar with goblet cells in the fornix/palpebral parts).
questions.keyConcept: Bulbar conjunctiva is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium.
options: Stratif. Columnar epithelium with goblet cells.
Stratifed cubical epithelium with goblet cells.

questions.text: The main refractive media of the eye is:
questions.explanation: Because of the large refractive-index difference between air and tissue at the air-cornea interface, the cornea provides about two-thirds of the eye's refractive power, making it the main refractive medium.
questions.keyConcept: The cornea is the main refractive medium of the eye.

questions.text: Cataract is the opacity of:
questions.explanation: A cataract is loss of transparency of the lens, usually from age-related changes in lens fibre proteins.
questions.keyConcept: Cataract = opacity (loss of transparency) of the lens.

questions.text: Decreased lens elasticity causes:
questions.explanation: With age the lens loses elasticity and can no longer round up for near vision; this age-related decline in accommodation is presbyopia.
questions.keyConcept: Loss of lens elasticity with age impairs near focus = presbyopia.

questions.text: Aqueous veins:
questions.explanation: Aqueous veins drain aqueous humour out of the canal of Schlemm into the episcleral venous system; they contain aqueous humour (which mixes with blood more peripherally).
questions.keyConcept: Aqueous veins carry aqueous humour from the canal of Schlemm to episcleral veins.

questions.text: Which is the most vascular part in the eye?
questions.explanation: The choroid carries the choriocapillaris and is the most vascular coat of the eye. (No answer was marked on the source page; inferred with high confidence and consistent with the circled version of this question earlier in the file.)
questions.keyConcept: The choroid is the most vascular part of the eye.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered the main refractive media of the eye?
questions.explanation: The air-cornea interface supplies most of the eye's refractive power, so the cornea is the main refractive medium. (No answer was marked on the source page; inferred with high confidence and consistent with the circled version of this question earlier in the file.)
questions.keyConcept: The cornea is the main refractive medium of the eye.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of the optic disc?
questions.explanation: The optic disc lacks photoreceptors and is the blind spot, hence insensitive to light; retinal vessels actually enter at the disc. (No answer was marked on the source page; inferred with high confidence and consistent with the circled version of this question earlier in the file.)
questions.keyConcept: The optic disc has no photoreceptors, so it is insensitive to light (blind spot).
options: The site of maximum visual acuity.
Where condensation of photoreceptors is found.

questions.text: The lacrimal sac is lined with which of the following types of epithelium?
questions.explanation: The lacrimal sac and nasolacrimal duct are lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium. (No answer was marked on the source page; inferred with high confidence and consistent with the printed answer key of the Part 2 eye question on the lacrimal sac.)
questions.keyConcept: The lacrimal sac is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium.

questions.text: Outer phalangeal cell:
questions.explanation: Outer phalangeal (Deiters) cells support the outer hair cells; the fluid-filled spaces of Nuel lie between them and the outer hair cells. They do not surround hair cells completely.
questions.keyConcept: Outer phalangeal (Deiters) cells are separated by the spaces of Nuel.

questions.text: The tectorial membrane is formed by:
questions.explanation: The acellular tectorial membrane overlying the organ of Corti is secreted by the interdental cells that cover the spiral limbus.
questions.keyConcept: The tectorial membrane is secreted by the interdental cells of the spiral limbus.

questions.text: Hair cell in macula differ than hair cells in organ of corti in having:
questions.explanation: Vestibular hair cells (maculae and cristae) possess a single true kinocilium plus stereocilia, whereas mature cochlear hair cells in the organ of Corti lack a kinocilium.
questions.keyConcept: Vestibular (macular) hair cells keep a kinocilium; cochlear hair cells lose it.

questions.text: Interdental cells present in:
questions.explanation: Interdental cells are located on the spiral limbus, where they secrete and maintain the tectorial membrane.
questions.keyConcept: Interdental cells sit on the spiral limbus and secrete the tectorial membrane.

questions.text: Ion transporting cells present in:
questions.explanation: The stria vascularis on the lateral wall of the cochlear duct is a vascularized ion-transporting epithelium responsible for secreting the K+-rich endolymph.
questions.keyConcept: The stria vascularis is the ion-transporting epithelium that produces endolymph.

questions.text: Perilymph is formed from micro-vessels in:
questions.explanation: Perilymph (similar to extracellular fluid, low K+/high Na+) is derived from the microvasculature of the periosteum lining the bony labyrinth; endolymph instead comes from the stria vascularis.
questions.keyConcept: Perilymph is formed from microvessels of the periosteum lining the bony labyrinth.

questions.text: Crista ampullaris is differ than maculae in having:
questions.explanation: The crista ampullaris is covered by the cupula, a tall gelatinous mass without otoliths, sensing angular acceleration. The maculae instead carry an otolithic membrane with otoliths.
questions.keyConcept: The crista ampullaris is capped by a gelatinous cupula (no otoliths), unlike the maculae.

questions.text: Supporting cells of receptor areas have apical few:
questions.explanation: The columnar supporting cells of the maculae and cristae carry a few apical microvilli, in contrast to the stereocilia/kinocilium of the hair cells.
questions.keyConcept: Supporting cells of the sensory areas bear a few apical microvilli.

questions.text: Type I hair cell differ than type II in macula by having:
questions.explanation: Type I vestibular hair cells are flask/amphora-shaped and are surrounded by a goblet/chalice (club)-shaped afferent nerve terminal. Type II cells are cylindrical with bouton endings. Both share mitochondria, Golgi, kinocilium and stereocilia.
questions.keyConcept: Type I vestibular hair cells are flask-shaped, enclosed by a club-/chalice-shaped afferent nerve calyx.
options: Flask shape with a club shape afferent.

questions.text: Otolithic membrane is formed by:
questions.explanation: The gelatinous otolithic membrane, studded with otoliths (otoconia), is produced by the supporting cells of the maculae of the utricle and saccule.
questions.keyConcept: The otolithic membrane is secreted by the supporting cells of the maculae.

questions.text: Tensor tympani muscle is ............ & attached to ............
questions.explanation: The tensor tympani is a skeletal muscle that inserts on the handle of the malleus and tenses the tympanic membrane to dampen loud sounds. (The stapedius attaches to the stapes.)
questions.keyConcept: Tensor tympani is a skeletal muscle inserting on the malleus.

questions.text: Middle layer of tympanic membrane is formed of:
questions.explanation: The tympanic membrane has an outer skin layer, an inner mucosal layer, and a middle fibrous layer of radial and circular collagen fibres together with elastic fibres.
questions.keyConcept: The middle (fibrous) layer of the eardrum is made of collagen & elastic fibers.

questions.text: Ceruminous glands are:
questions.explanation: Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine sweat glands in the wall of the external auditory meatus; with sebaceous glands they produce cerumen (ear wax).
questions.keyConcept: Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine sweat glands of the external auditory meatus.

questions.text: Respiratory tract infection can reach the tympanic cavity through:
questions.explanation: The Eustachian (auditory) tube connects the nasopharynx with the middle ear, so upper respiratory infections can ascend it to cause otitis media.
questions.keyConcept: Infection spreads from the nasopharynx to the middle ear via the Eustachian (auditory) tube.

questions.text: The vestibule contains:
questions.explanation: The vestibule is the central part of the bony labyrinth and contains the membranous utricle and saccule. The semicircular canals and cochlea open into it.
questions.keyConcept: The vestibule of the bony labyrinth houses the utricle and saccule.

questions.text: Sensory part of the saccule is covered by:
questions.explanation: The sensory area of the saccule is the macula, whose hair cells are embedded in the otolithic membrane carrying otoliths for linear acceleration/gravity sensing.
questions.keyConcept: The macula of the saccule is covered by the otolithic membrane.

questions.text: The vestibular apparatus is responsible for:
questions.explanation: The vestibular apparatus (maculae + cristae) detects head orientation, linear and angular acceleration, providing the sense of equilibrium, so all options apply.
questions.keyConcept: The vestibular apparatus handles equilibrium, head orientation and angular acceleration.
options: Orientation of the head in space.

questions.text: Which part of the inner ear gives impulses when one falls down:
questions.explanation: The utricular macula lies horizontally and detects horizontal linear acceleration and head tilt; per the source key it signals when one falls. The saccular macula is vertical and the crista detects angular acceleration.
questions.keyConcept: The macula of the utricle senses horizontal linear acceleration (e.g. falling forward).

questions.text: Hair cells of the crista ampullaris are characterized by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hair cells of the crista have a single kinocilium, are embedded in the cupula and sense angular acceleration, but they do not rest on the basement membrane - they sit on the supporting cells, which contact the basal lamina.
questions.keyConcept: Crista hair cells do NOT reach the basement membrane; only supporting cells rest on it.

questions.text: Hair cells have:
questions.explanation: Hair cells contain mitochondria and Golgi, bear apical stereocilia, and are contacted basally by both afferent and efferent nerve endings, so all options apply.
questions.keyConcept: Hair cells possess organelles, apical stereocilia and basal afferent & efferent endings.

questions.text: Oval window is characterized by all the following except:
questions.explanation: The oval window links the middle and inner ear and is occupied by the stapes footplate. Relief of sound-wave pressure is the function of the round (secondary) window, so that option is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Pressure relief is the round window's role; the oval window holds the stapes footplate.
options: Connect the middle ear to the inner ear.
Attached to the foot plate of stapes.
Relieves the pressure of sound waves.

questions.text: All of the following about the basilar membrane is true except:
questions.explanation: The basilar membrane carries the organ of Corti, stretches from the spiral limbus to the spiral ligament, and is narrowest (stiffest) at the cochlear base. It separates the cochlear duct (scala media) from the scala tympani, so the statement about scala vestibuli is false.
questions.keyConcept: Basilar membrane separates scala media from scala tympani - NOT scala tympani from scala vestibuli.
options: Extends from the spiral ligament to the spiral limbus.
Separates scala tympani from the scala vestibuli.
Narrowest at the base of the cochlea.

questions.text: The superficial cells of corneal epithelium have:
questions.explanation: The corneal epithelium is stratified squamous non-keratinized; its superficial cells carry microvilli (microplicae) that retain the tear film. It is not keratinized.
questions.keyConcept: Superficial corneal epithelial cells bear microvilli that stabilize the tear film.

questions.text: The corneal epithelium has many:
questions.explanation: The corneal epithelium is densely supplied with free sensory nerve endings, making the cornea extremely sensitive. It is avascular, which is also why it has no blood vessels.
questions.keyConcept: The cornea is richly innervated (very sensitive) but avascular.

questions.text: Corneal transplantation is successful due to:
questions.explanation: The cornea's lack of blood and lymphatic vessels limits immune access to the graft, giving immune privilege and a high success rate for corneal transplantation.
questions.keyConcept: Corneal grafts succeed because the avascular cornea is immune-privileged.

questions.text: One of the following is the cause of opacity of sclera:
questions.explanation: Unlike the regularly spaced lamellae of the transparent cornea, the sclera's collagen bundles run in irregular directions and sizes, scattering light and making it opaque (white).
questions.keyConcept: The sclera is opaque because its collagen fibres are irregularly arranged.

questions.text: What is the change of the Descemet's membrane at limbus:
questions.explanation: At the limbus the corneal Descemet's membrane splits into strands forming the pectinate ligament (trabecular meshwork) of the iridocorneal angle.
questions.keyConcept: At the limbus Descemet's membrane breaks up into the pectinate ligament of the angle.

questions.text: What is the change of the Descemet's endothelium at limbus:
questions.explanation: At the angle the corneal (Descemet's) endothelium becomes continuous with the cells lining the trabecular spaces of Fontana, through which aqueous drains to the canal of Schlemm.
questions.keyConcept: The corneal endothelium continues at the limbus to line the spaces of Fontana.

questions.text: The episcleral tissue is formed of:
questions.explanation: The episclera is the outer connective-tissue layer of the sclera; the source answer key designates it as fibroelastic connective tissue (a loose, vascular fibroelastic layer).
questions.keyConcept: Per the source key, the episcleral tissue is fibroelastic connective tissue.

questions.text: The lamina fusca of sclera is formed of:
questions.explanation: The lamina fusca is the innermost scleral layer adjacent to the choroid; it contains melanocytes, making it pigmented connective tissue.
questions.keyConcept: The lamina fusca is the inner pigmented layer of the sclera (melanocyte-rich).

questions.text: Bruch's membrane is found in:
questions.explanation: Bruch's membrane forms the inner boundary of the choroid, lying between the choriocapillaris and the retinal pigment epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Bruch's membrane is the innermost layer of the choroid, next to the RPE.

questions.text: The central core of Bruch's membrane is formed of:
questions.explanation: Bruch's membrane is five-layered: the central core is a sheet of elastic fibres, flanked by inner and outer collagen layers and the basal laminae of the RPE and choriocapillaris.
questions.keyConcept: Bruch's membrane has a central elastic-fibre layer between two collagen layers.

questions.text: Suprachoroid layer is formed of:
questions.explanation: The suprachoroid (lamina fusca side) is the outermost choroidal layer, made of thin collagen and elastic lamellae interspersed with melanocytes and fibroblasts.
questions.keyConcept: The suprachoroid is collagen & elastic lamellae with melanocytes.

questions.text: Ciliary epithelium basal membrane shows:
questions.explanation: The non-pigmented ciliary epithelium that secretes aqueous humour shows extensive basal and lateral membrane infoldings typical of ion-transporting cells.
questions.keyConcept: Ciliary (non-pigmented) epithelium shows basal membrane infoldings for ion transport.

questions.text: The anterior surface of iris is covered by:
questions.explanation: The anterior surface of the iris is not a true epithelium; it is a discontinuous layer of fibroblasts and melanocytes (pigment cells) overlying the stroma.
questions.keyConcept: The anterior iris surface is an incomplete layer of fibroblasts & pigment cells (melanocytes).

questions.text: The myo-epithelial cells in iris are differentiating from:
questions.explanation: The dilator pupillae is formed by myoepithelial (myoid) processes of the anterior/outer layer of the two-layered posterior pigmented iris epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Iris dilator myoepithelium arises from the outer (anterior) layer of the posterior iris epithelium.

questions.text: Pigmented epithelium of retina form vitamin A due to presence of:
questions.explanation: Retinal pigment epithelial cells contain abundant smooth endoplasmic reticulum used to esterify and regenerate vitamin A (retinoids) for the visual cycle.
questions.keyConcept: The RPE's abundant SER handles vitamin A (retinoid) metabolism for the visual cycle.

questions.text: Pigmented epithelium of retina essential for turn over of rods as it has:
questions.explanation: The RPE phagocytoses the tips of shed rod outer-segment discs and digests them using its abundant lysosomes, which is essential for photoreceptor renewal/turnover.
questions.keyConcept: RPE lysosomes phagocytose and digest shed rod outer-segment discs (disc turnover).

questions.text: Rods is differ than cones in having:
questions.explanation: Rod discs are separate from the plasma membrane and are continuously shed and renewed (high turnover). Discs continuous with the cell membrane and flat synaptic pedicles are features of cones.
questions.keyConcept: Rod outer-segment discs show high turnover (continuous shedding & renewal).
options: A flat pedicle at synaptic region.
Membranous discs continuous with cell membrane.

questions.text: Diffuse bipolar cells synapse with:
questions.explanation: Diffuse bipolar cells collect signals from many rods (high convergence), which underlies the rods' high sensitivity but low acuity.
questions.keyConcept: Diffuse (rod) bipolar cells receive input from many rod cells.

questions.text: Midget bipolar nerve cell synapse with:
questions.explanation: In the foveal midget pathway a single cone connects through a midget bipolar cell to a single (midget) ganglion cell, giving high visual acuity. Per the options, it synapses with a single ganglion cell.
questions.keyConcept: Midget bipolar cells form a one-to-one line, synapsing with a single ganglion cell.

questions.text: Retinal detachments means separation at line between:
questions.explanation: The potential space between the RPE and the neural retina (the embryonic optic-cup cavity) is where retinal detachment occurs, separating the pigment epithelium from the rest of the retina.
questions.keyConcept: Retinal detachment separates the neural retina from the retinal pigment epithelium.
options: Pigmented epithelium & other layers of retina.
Outer limiting membrane & outer nuclear layer.
Ganglion cell layer & optic nerve layer.
Inner nuclear layer & inner plexiform layer.

questions.text: Lacrimal sac lined by:
questions.explanation: The lacrimal sac and nasolacrimal duct are lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium continuous with the nasal respiratory mucosa.
questions.keyConcept: The lacrimal sac is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium.

questions.text: Lacrimal canaliculus lined by:
questions.explanation: The lacrimal canaliculi (draining tears from the puncta to the lacrimal sac) are lined by stratified squamous epithelium, continuous with the conjunctival lining.
questions.keyConcept: The lacrimal canaliculi are lined by stratified squamous epithelium.

questions.text: Fovea centralis in retina characterized by:
questions.explanation: The fovea centralis is a cone-only, avascular pit where other retinal layers are displaced aside, giving the sharpest (highest-acuity) vision.
questions.keyConcept: The fovea contains only cones and gives maximum visual acuity (and is avascular).

questions.text: Concerning ora serrata, it has:
questions.explanation: The ora serrata is the serrated anterior margin of the neural retina; here the retina becomes very thin and reduced largely to Muller cells, with loss of photoreceptors and neurons.
questions.keyConcept: At the ora serrata the retina thins to mainly Muller cells (photoreceptors/neurons disappear).

questions.text: The inner blood retinal barrier is formed by tight junction between:
questions.explanation: The inner blood-retinal barrier is formed by zonulae occludentes between the endothelial cells of the non-fenestrated retinal capillaries. (The outer barrier is between RPE cells.)
questions.keyConcept: Inner blood-retinal barrier = tight junctions between retinal capillary endothelial cells.
options: Endothelial cells of retinal blood capillaries.

questions.text: The main refractive media in eye is:
questions.explanation: The air-cornea interface provides most of the refractive power of the eye, so the cornea is the principal refractive medium.
questions.keyConcept: The cornea is the main refractive medium of the eye.

questions.text: Lens capsule is formed of:
questions.explanation: The lens capsule is an exceptionally thick basement membrane secreted by the lens epithelium, rich in type IV collagen and glycoproteins.
questions.keyConcept: The lens capsule is a thick basement membrane (type IV collagen + glycoprotein).

questions.text: Lens fibers are:
questions.explanation: Lens fibres are elongated, highly differentiated epithelial cells that lose their nuclei and organelles and fill with crystallin proteins for transparency.
questions.keyConcept: Lens fibers are highly differentiated epithelial cells packed with crystallins.

questions.text: Concerning the sub-capsular epithelium of lens, which of the followings is true:
questions.explanation: The lens has a single layer of cuboidal subcapsular epithelium on its anterior surface only; at the equator these cells proliferate and differentiate into new lens fibres throughout life.
questions.keyConcept: The anterior subcapsular lens epithelium divides at the equator and differentiates into lens fibers.
options: Formed of 2 layers of cuboidal cell.
Cover anterior & posterior surface of lens.

questions.text: In old age, the lens become less transparent due to:
questions.explanation: With aging, brown (lipochrome) pigments accumulate within the lens fibres and the proteins aggregate, reducing transparency and producing senile (nuclear) cataract.
questions.keyConcept: Age-related lens opacity results from brown pigment accumulating in the lens fibers.
options: Accumulation of brown pigments in its fibers.
Accumulation of brown pigments in its epithelium.

questions.text: Ganglion cell layer contains:
questions.explanation: The ganglion cell layer contains the cell bodies of the multipolar ganglion neurons together with supporting neuroglia and branches of the central retinal vessels, so all options apply.
questions.keyConcept: The ganglion cell layer holds multipolar ganglion neurons, neuroglia and blood vessels.

questions.text: Flat bipolar cells synapse with:
questions.explanation: Flat bipolar cells make superficial (flat) contacts with several photoreceptors; per the source they synapse with both rods and cones.
questions.keyConcept: Flat (diffuse) bipolar cells synapse with both rods and cones.

questions.text: Outer segment of rods is formed of:
questions.explanation: The rod outer segment is filled with hundreds of flattened membranous discs that have pinched off and are separate from the plasma membrane (unlike cones, whose discs stay continuous with it).
questions.keyConcept: Rod outer segments contain stacked membranous discs separate from (not continuous with) the cell membrane.
options: Membranous saccules that continuous with cell membrane.
Membranous saccules that not continuous with cell membrane.

questions.text: A patient undergoes LASIK surgery to correct myopia. Which layer of the cornea is primarily reshaped during this procedure, and what is its percentage of total corneal thickness?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Substantia propria, 90%.
questions.keyConcept: Substantia propria, 90%

questions.text: A researcher is studying corneal transparency. Which of the following combinations of features is essential for maintaining corneal clarity, as described in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Avascularity, regular arrangement of fibers, and continuous fluid withdrawal by endothelium.
questions.keyConcept: Avascularity, regular arrangement of fibers, and continuous fluid withdrawal by endothelium
options: High vascularity and regular collagen arrangement
Avascularity, regular arrangement of fibers, and continuous fluid withdrawal by endothelium
Presence of melanocytes and irregular collagen fibers
High water content and irregular fiber arrangement
Stratified squamous epithelium and microvilli on superficial cells

questions.text: A histologist examines a section of the cornea and identifies a thick, homogeneous, non-cellular layer beneath the epithelium. This layer is synthesized by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Corneal epithelium and stromal cells.
questions.keyConcept: Corneal epithelium and stromal cells

questions.text: Following a chemical injury, a patient's corneal epithelium is completely denuded. Regeneration of this epithelium relies primarily on stem cells located in which specific region?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: The limbus.
questions.keyConcept: The limbus

questions.text: A patient presents with a condition causing rapid corneal swelling and opacity due to metabolic damage. Which specific layer of the cornea is primarily compromised in this scenario?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Descemet's endothelium.
questions.keyConcept: Descemet's endothelium

questions.text: The high sensory innervation of the cornea is a key clinical feature. In which specific layer of the corneal epithelium are the numerous free nerve endings predominantly found?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Intermediate polygonal cell layers.
questions.keyConcept: Intermediate polygonal cell layers

questions.text: Which statement best explains the structural basis for the opacity of the sclera as contrasted with the transparency of the cornea?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Scleral fibers are irregularly arranged and have high water content, while corneal fibers are regularly arranged.
questions.keyConcept: Scleral fibers are irregularly arranged and have high water content, while corneal fibers are regularly arranged.
options: Sclera is avascular, whereas cornea is highly vascularized.
Scleral fibers are irregularly arranged and have high water content, while corneal fibers are regularly arranged.
Sclera has a stratified squamous epithelium, while cornea has simple epithelium.
Sclera lacks a Bowman's membrane equivalent.
Sclera contains melanocytes, which scatter light.

questions.text: A histological section at the corneoscleral junction (limbus) shows a splitting of Descemet's membrane to form a specific structure. This structure is the:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Trabecular meshwork (pectinate ligament).
questions.keyConcept: Trabecular meshwork (pectinate ligament)

questions.text: Spaces of fontana lined by which of the following cell types, reflecting its continuity with the corneal endothelium?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Descemet's endothelium.
questions.keyConcept: Descemet's endothelium

questions.text: The anterior chamber of the eye is bounded anteriorly by the cornea and posteriorly by the iris and lens. The posterior chamber lies between the posterior surface of the iris, the lens, and the suspensory ligament. Both chambers are filled with aqueous humor. Which chamber is directly adjacent to the vitreous body posteriorly?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Vitreous chamber.
questions.keyConcept: Vitreous chamber
options: None, as vitreous body is in the anterior chamber

questions.text: The sclera proper (substantia propria) is characterized by which type of connective tissue arrangement that contributes to its opacity and mechanical strength?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Dense irregular connective tissue with thick collagen fibers.
questions.keyConcept: Dense irregular connective tissue with thick collagen fibers
options: Loose connective tissue with elastic fibers
Dense irregular connective tissue with thick collagen fibers
Dense regular connective tissue with parallel collagen fibers
Reticular connective tissue with type III collagen

questions.text: Which of the following accurately pairs a corneal layer with its primary structural composition or origin?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Substantia propria - Collagen fibrils, keratocytes, and ground substance.
questions.keyConcept: Substantia propria - Collagen fibrils, keratocytes, and ground substance
options: Bowman's membrane - Type IV collagen network, synthesized by endothelium
Descemet's membrane - Type I collagen and intercellular substance, no cells
Substantia propria - Collagen fibrils, keratocytes, and ground substance
Corneal epithelium - Simple cuboidal epithelium with goblet cells
Descemet's endothelium - Stratified squamous epithelium with microvilli

questions.text: A researcher investigating the avascular nature of the cornea notes that its central region receives metabolites primarily from which source?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Aqueous humor.
questions.keyConcept: Aqueous humor

questions.text: The Tenon's capsule is a layer of dense connective tissue that is intimately associated with which structure of the outer fibrous layer?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Sclera proper (substantia propria).
questions.keyConcept: Sclera proper (substantia propria)

questions.text: At the iridocorneal angle, the trabecular meshwork encloses spaces known as the spaces of Fontana. These spaces are crucial for the drainage of aqueous humor into the:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Canal of Schlemm.
questions.keyConcept: Canal of Schlemm

questions.text: The stem cells located at the limbus are responsible for the centripetal movement of progenitor cells onto the cornea. What important barrier function does this movement create?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Blocks migration of conjunctival epithelium onto the cornea.
questions.keyConcept: Blocks migration of conjunctival epithelium onto the cornea
options: Blocks migration of conjunctival epithelium onto the cornea

questions.text: Which layer of the sclera contains melanocytes and is separated from the choroid by the perichoroidal space?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Suprachoroid Lamina fusca.
questions.keyConcept: Suprachoroid Lamina fusca

questions.text: The optic nerve passes through a perforation in the sclera posteriorly. At this point, the sclera is continuous with which covering of the optic nerve?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Epineurium.
questions.keyConcept: Epineurium

questions.text: The microvilli on the superficial cells of the corneal epithelium serve a critical function in maintaining the corneal surface by:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Retaining a film of tears to keep the cornea wet.
questions.keyConcept: Retaining a film of tears to keep the cornea wet
options: Retaining a film of tears to keep the cornea wet
Anchoring the epithelium to Bowman's membrane

questions.text: Which of the following is a true statement regarding the layers of the cornea?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: The stroma constitutes 90% of corneal thickness.
questions.keyConcept: The stroma constitutes 90% of corneal thickness.
options: Bowman's membrane is the basement membrane of the endothelium.
Descemet's membrane is synthesized by the corneal epithelium.
The stroma constitutes 90% of corneal thickness.
The epithelium is a simple cuboidal layer.

questions.text: Bruch's membrane (lamina vitrea) separates the choriocapillaris from the retina. Which of the following correctly describes its layered composition?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Basal lamina of choriocapillaris endothelium, two collagen layers with an elastic layer between, and basal lamina of retinal pigment epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Basal lamina of choriocapillaris endothelium, two collagen layers with an elastic layer between, and basal lamina of re…
options: Single basement membrane of the retinal pigment epithelium
Basal lamina of choriocapillaris endothelium, two collagen layers with an elastic layer between, and basal lamina of retinal pigment epithelium
Loose connective tissue with melanocytes and elastic fibers
Dense irregular collagenous tissue with fibroblasts
A single layer of pigmented epithelial cells

questions.text: The ciliary muscle is responsible for visual accommodation. The origin of all three bundles of ciliary muscle is the:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Scleral spur at the limbus.
questions.keyConcept: Scleral spur at the limbus

questions.text: The inner non-pigmented layer of the ciliary epithelium exhibits ultrastructural features indicative of active ion transport and secretion. Which of the following features is specifically mentioned in the lecture as characteristic of these cells?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Basal membrane infoldings with elongated mitochondria and Na-K ATPase in lateral membranes.
questions.keyConcept: Basal membrane infoldings with elongated mitochondria and Na-K ATPase in lateral membranes
options: Basal membrane infoldings with elongated mitochondria and Na-K ATPase in lateral membranes
Transverse striations due to stacked membranous discs

questions.text: The ciliary processes secrete aqueous humor. The inner non-pigmented epithelium is also responsible for secreting which structural component that suspends the lens?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Zonular fibers (suspensory ligament).
questions.keyConcept: Zonular fibers (suspensory ligament)

questions.text: The dilator pupillae muscle is described histologically as not being a true muscle. Instead, it is formed by:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Myoepithelial cells extending from the basal lamina of the outer pigmented epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Myoepithelial cells extending from the basal lamina of the outer pigmented epithelium
options: Skeletal muscle fibers from the ciliary body
Myoepithelial cells extending from the basal lamina of the outer pigmented epithelium
A condensation of collagen fibers in the iris stroma

questions.text: The posterior surface of the iris is lined by two layers of pigmented cuboidal epithelium. The primary function of this heavy pigmentation is to:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Block light from entering the eye except through the pupil.
questions.keyConcept: Block light from entering the eye except through the pupil
options: Provide structural support to the iris stroma
Block light from entering the eye except through the pupil
Synthesize the limiting membrane of the iris

questions.text: Which structure is the most anterior extension of the choroid, forming a colored, discshaped diaphragm?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Iris.
questions.keyConcept: Iris

questions.text: The constrictor pupillae muscle is located in which layer of the iris, and what is its effect on pupil diameter?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Vessel layer (stroma) periphery; constricts pupil.
questions.keyConcept: Vessel layer (stroma) periphery; constricts pupil
options: Limiting membrane; no effect on diameter

questions.text: The blood-aqueous barrier is formed by tight junctions between which specific cells?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Inner non-pigmented cells of ciliary epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Inner non-pigmented cells of ciliary epithelium
options: Endothelial cells of ciliary body capillaries
Outer pigmented cells of ciliary epithelium
Inner non-pigmented cells of ciliary epithelium

questions.text: Tenon’s capsule allows for:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Rotatory movement of the eye.
questions.keyConcept: Rotatory movement of the eye
options: The potential space for retinal detachment
The path for aqueous humor drainage
The location of the canal of Schlemm

questions.text: Which of the following cell types is found in the ciliary body stroma alongside blood vessels and melanocytes?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Ciliary muscle fibers.
questions.keyConcept: Ciliary muscle fibers

questions.text: The outer pigmented layer of the ciliary epithelium is a continuation of which retinal layer?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Pigmented epithelium of the retina.
questions.keyConcept: Pigmented epithelium of the retina

questions.text: The function of the ciliary muscle is visual accommodation. Contraction of this muscle affects the lens by:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Relaxing tension on the suspensory ligament (zonule).
questions.keyConcept: Relaxing tension on the suspensory ligament (zonule)
options: Directly pulling on the lens capsule
Relaxing tension on the suspensory ligament (zonule)
Increasing tension on the suspensory ligament
Changing the curvature of the cornea

questions.text: Regarding the choroid's choriocapillary layer, its primary function is to:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Nourish the outer layers of the retina (photoreceptors).
questions.keyConcept: Nourish the outer layers of the retina (photoreceptors)
options: Nourish the outer layers of the retina (photoreceptors)

questions.text: A patient presents with glaucoma due to impaired drainage of aqueous humor. The obstruction is most likely at the level of which structures located in the iridocorneal angle?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Trabecular meshwork and canal of Schlemm.
questions.keyConcept: Trabecular meshwork and canal of Schlemm
options: Trabecular meshwork and canal of Schlemm

questions.text: The wedge-shaped ciliary body in cross-section has three surfaces. Which surface contains the ciliary processes and faces the lens and posterior chamber?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Medial surface.
questions.keyConcept: Medial surface

questions.text: Melanocytes in the choroid and ciliary body contribute to the light-proofing of the eye. In the iris, the color of the eye is determined by the:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Number and distribution of melanocytes in the iris stroma and anterior surface.
questions.keyConcept: Number and distribution of melanocytes in the iris stroma and anterior surface
options: Amount of rhodopsin in the photoreceptors
Number and distribution of melanocytes in the iris stroma and anterior surface
Thickness of the posterior pigmented epithelium
Presence of lipofuscin in the dilator pupillae

questions.text: The pigmented epithelium of the retina plays a critical role in the visual cycle by esterifying Vitamin A. Which organelle is specifically mentioned as the site of this process?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (sER).
questions.keyConcept: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (sER)

questions.text: The membranous discs in the outer segment of rod cells contain the photosensitive pigment rhodopsin. A key ultrastructural difference between rod discs and cone discs is that:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Cone discs are continuous with the cell membrane, rod discs are not.
questions.keyConcept: Cone discs are continuous with the cell membrane, rod discs are not.
options: Rod discs are continuous with the cell membrane, cone discs are not.
Cone discs are continuous with the cell membrane, rod discs are not.
Rod discs are stacked vertically, cone discs are horizontal.
Rod discs are phagocytosed by Muller cells, cone discs by pigmented epithelium.

questions.text: The outer limiting membrane of the retina is formed by:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Tight junctions and zonula adherens between Muller cells and photoreceptors.
questions.keyConcept: Tight junctions and zonula adherens between Muller cells and photoreceptors
options: Tight junctions and zonula adherens between Muller cells and photoreceptors
The basal lamina of Muller cells
A condensation of collagen fibers from the choroid
The apical microvilli of pigmented epithelial cells
The synapses in the outer plexiform layer

questions.text: Which of the following cell types in the inner nuclear layer has dendrites that synapse exclusively with cones, and axons that synapse with both rods and cones, functioning in the integration of stimuli?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Horizontal cells.
questions.keyConcept: Horizontal cells

questions.text: The fovea centralis is an area of highest visual acuity. Which of the following histological features is characteristic of the fovea?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Divergence of inner retinal layers (layers 4-9) to the sides, exposing closely packed cones.
questions.keyConcept: Divergence of inner retinal layers (layers 4-9) to the sides, exposing closely packed cones
options: Presence of both rods and cones, with a high density of rods
Divergence of inner retinal layers (layers 4-9) to the sides, exposing closely packed cones
High concentration of blood vessels for nutrient supply

questions.text: The optic disc (optic papilla) is also known as the blind spot. The absence of which specific layer is directly responsible for its insensitivity to light?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Photoreceptor layer (rods and cones).
questions.keyConcept: Photoreceptor layer (rods and cones)

questions.text: Muller cells are the principal neuroglial cells of the retina. Their processes extend from the internal limiting membrane to the external limiting membrane. Which of the following functions is NOT attributed to Muller cells based on the lecture?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Phagocytosing shed outer segment discs.
questions.keyConcept: Phagocytosing shed outer segment discs
options: Forming the retinal scaffold for support
Contributing to the internal limiting membrane

questions.text: The inner segment of a photoreceptor is divided into an ellipsoid and myoid portion. The ellipsoid is characterized by the presence of which structures essential for energy production?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Basal body of the cilium and mitochondria.
questions.keyConcept: Basal body of the cilium and mitochondria
options: Basal body of the cilium and mitochondria

questions.text: The connecting stalk between the outer and inner segment of a photoreceptor is considered a modified cilium. What is the microtubule arrangement described for this structure?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: 9 peripheral doublets, no central singlet.
questions.keyConcept: 9 peripheral doublets, no central singlet

questions.text: The synaptic region of a rod cell is a spherule that contacts dendrites of bipolar cells and axons of horizontal cells. In contrast, the synaptic terminal of a cone cell is a:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Pedicle with short processes.
questions.keyConcept: Pedicle with short processes

questions.text: The blood-retinal barrier is formed by lateral junctional complexes between cells of which layer?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Retinal pigmented epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Retinal pigmented epithelium

questions.text: The inner plexiform layer of the retina is the site of synapses between which three neuronal types?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Bipolar cells, amacrine cells, ganglion cells.
questions.keyConcept: Bipolar cells, amacrine cells, ganglion cells
options: Bipolar cells, amacrine cells, ganglion cells

questions.text: The outer nuclear layer contains the nuclei of rods and cones. How are the rod and cone nuclei distributed within this layer?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Cone nuclei are in a single row near the external limiting membrane; rod nuclei are more numerous and in several levels.
questions.keyConcept: Cone nuclei are in a single row near the external limiting membrane; rod nuclei are more numerous and in several levels.
options: Both are in a single row close to the external limiting membrane.
Cone nuclei are in a single row near the external limiting membrane; rod nuclei are more numerous and in several levels.
Rod nuclei are in a single row; cone nuclei are scattered in several levels.
Both are randomly distributed throughout the layer.
Cone nuclei are located closer to the outer plexiform layer.

questions.text: The pigmented epithelial cells have apical microvilli that embrace the outer segments of rods and cones. Which of the following is a function of these microvilli?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: They contain melanin pigments to absorb light.
questions.keyConcept: They contain melanin pigments to absorb light.
options: They are firmly attached to photoreceptors to prevent detachment.
They contain melanin pigments to absorb light.

questions.text: Phagocytosis of shed outer segment discs is a critical function of the retinal pigmented epithelium. Which organelle is responsible for digesting these phagocytosed discs?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Lysosomes.
questions.keyConcept: Lysosomes

questions.text: Amacrine cells, located in the inner part of the inner nuclear layer, are unique because they:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Have dendrites only; no axons.
questions.keyConcept: Have dendrites only; no axons.
options: Have a long axon projecting to the brain.
Are the primary photoreceptors for color vision.

questions.text: The optic nerve fiber layer contains axons of ganglion cells. A notable histological feature of these axons within the retina is that they are:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Non-myelinated.
questions.keyConcept: Non-myelinated
options: Surrounded by a dense connective tissue sheath
Continuous with the internal limiting membrane

questions.text: The turnover rate of rod outer segment discs, involving shedding and phagocytosis by pigmented epithelium, is given as an average of:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: 10 days. (Turnover rate = 9-13 days, average 10 days)
questions.keyConcept: 10 days

questions.text: The ora serrata represents the anterior border of the retina. At this junction, the neural retina transitions to:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: The ciliary body epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: The ciliary body epithelium

questions.text: The external limiting membrane is formed by junctions between Muller cells and which adjacent structures?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Rods and cones.
questions.keyConcept: Rods and cones

questions.text: The pigmented epithelium cells exhibit basal membrane infoldings with numerous mitochondria. This ultrastructural feature is characteristic of cells involved in:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Ion transport.
questions.keyConcept: Ion transport

questions.text: The number of rod cells in each retina is approximately 92 million, whereas cone cells number about 4.6 million. This numerical difference correlates with which functional specialization?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Cones are responsible for high visual acuity, rods for dim light perception.
questions.keyConcept: Cones are responsible for high visual acuity, rods for dim light perception.
options: Cones are responsible for high visual acuity, rods for dim light perception.
Rods are responsible for color vision, cones for black and white.
Cones are more numerous in the periphery, rods in the fovea.
Rods have a faster response time than cones.
Cones have a higher turnover rate of discs.

questions.text: The ganglion cell layer contains multipolar neurons. The "midget" (monosynaptic) ganglion cells are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Synapsing with a single cone bipolar cell.
questions.keyConcept: Synapsing with a single cone bipolar cell
options: Synapsing with multiple bipolar cells from rod pathways
Synapsing with a single cone bipolar cell
Being located in the outer nuclear layer

questions.text: Which of the following is a function of the pigmented epithelium in protecting the retina?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Absorption of light by melanin granules to prevent glaring and dazzling.
questions.keyConcept: Absorption of light by melanin granules to prevent glaring and dazzling
options: Absorption of light by melanin granules to prevent glaring and dazzling
Secretion of aqueous humor to maintain pressure
Synthesis of collagen for Bruch's membrane
Generation of action potentials in response to light

questions.text: The nuclei of cone cells are described as being:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Larger, less dense, and lying just internal to the outer limiting membrane.
questions.keyConcept: Larger, less dense, and lying just internal to the outer limiting membrane
options: Smaller, denser, and located deep in the outer nuclear layer
Larger, less dense, and lying just internal to the outer limiting membrane
Similar in appearance and location to rod nuclei
Located in the inner nuclear layer

questions.text: The photosensitive pigment in cones is iodopsin. A key property of cone pigment turnover compared to rods is that it has a:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Slower turnover rate (less turnover rate than rods).
questions.keyConcept: Slower turnover rate (less turnover rate than rods)
options: Slower turnover rate (less turnover rate than rods)

questions.text: The retinal blood vessels enter and exit the eye through which structure?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Optic disc.
questions.keyConcept: Optic disc

questions.text: The limiting membrane of the iris is a basal lamina covering the posterior inner surface. Which cells produce this membrane?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Posterior pigmented epithelium of the iris.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior pigmented epithelium of the iris
options: Posterior pigmented epithelium of the iris

questions.text: The lens capsule is described as a very thick, elastic, transparent basement membrane. Subcapsular epithelium is found only on which surface of the lens?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Anterior surface.
questions.keyConcept: Anterior surface

questions.text: As lens fibers mature and are pushed toward the center of the lens, they undergo a specific change: they lose their nuclei and organelles and become filled with:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Crystallin protein.
questions.keyConcept: Crystallin protein

questions.text: The vitreous body is composed of 99% water, collagen, hyaluronic acid, and a few cells (hyalocytes). The hyaloid canal traversing its center is a remnant of which embryonic structure?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Hyaloid artery.
questions.keyConcept: Hyaloid artery

questions.text: The bulbar conjunctiva is lined by which type of epithelium, and how does this differ from the palpebral conjunctiva?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Bulbar: non-keratinized stratified squamous; Palpebral: stratified columnar with goblet cells.
questions.keyConcept: Bulbar: non-keratinized stratified squamous; Palpebral: stratified columnar with goblet cells
options: Bulbar: stratified columnar with goblet cells; Palpebral: non-keratinized stratified squamous
Bulbar: non-keratinized stratified squamous; Palpebral: stratified columnar with goblet cells
Both are stratified columnar with goblet cells
Bulbar: simple cuboidal; Palpebral: stratified squamous

questions.text: Meibomian glands are located within the tarsal plate of the eyelid. They are modified sebaceous glands whose secretion functions to:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Prevent evaporation of tears.
questions.keyConcept: Prevent evaporation of tears

questions.text: Inflammation of the Meibomian glands or glands of Zeis can lead to a specific eyelid lesion. The lecture mentions "Chalazion" in association with which glands?
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Meibomian glands (modified sebaceous glands in tarsal plate).
questions.keyConcept: Meibomian glands (modified sebaceous glands in tarsal plate)
options: Glands of Zeis (modified sebaceous glands of eyelashes)
Meibomian glands (modified sebaceous glands in tarsal plate)

questions.text: The drainage pathway for tears begins at the lacrimal punctum and proceeds through the lacrimal canaliculus. The epithelium lining the lacrimal canaliculus is:
questions.explanation: Per the lecture answer key, the correct choice is: Stratified squamous epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Stratified squamous epithelium
options: Pseudostratified columnar ciliated epithelium with goblet cells

questions.text: The epithelium lining the lacrimal sac and nasolacrimal duct is described as:
